openObjectives.prompt: Ambrose has ruled a page into hours and is starting at the top. Tell Ambrose at what time you wake up or get up, using Italian.
Ambrose is sorting your habits into piles and the pile marked ALWAYS is empty. Tell Ambrose something that you always or often do, using Italian.
Ask Ambrose what they do in their free time, using Italian.

character.name: Ambrose Wattle
character.description: A broad figure built like a cupboard in an apron stiff with official starch, holding a clipboard like a shield. Ambrose is a Timetable Poet and writes verse in which everything happens at a stated hour and nothing rhymes with breakfast.

npc.narrative: You step into the radura under the stelle, where a lanterna sits on a sgabello beside a grande libro. Ambrose Wattle has a matita behind each orecchio and writes in the buio with great fiducia. A cartello on the albero says the clearing was better before the last reorganisation.
npc.native: Buonasera, io sono Ambrose Wattle, poeta degli orari. Mi sveglio alle cinque, mi alzo alle cinque e un minuto, e sempre scrivo una poesia. Spesso uso il mio tempo libero per contare le stelle. E tu, a che ora inizia la tua giornata, e cosa fai di solito quando la notte è tranquilla?
npc.translation: Good evening, I am Ambrose Wattle, poet of timetables. I wake up at five, I get up at one minute past five, and I always write a poem. I often use my free time to count the stars. And you, at what time does your day begin, and what do you usually do when the night is quiet?

player: Buonasera Ambrose! Io mi sveglio alle sette. Alle cinque? Troppo presto!

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Ambrose and told him clearly that you wake up at seven, and your joke about five o'clock being too early was good Italian too.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you told Ambrose when you wake up with "mi sveglio alle sette".
This one still needs doing: tell Ambrose something you always or often do. Ambrose will give you another chance to say it later.
Here you are asked to ask Ambrose what he does in his free time. Ambrose will bring this up again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Ambrose is sorting your habits into piles and the pile marked ALWAYS is empty. Tell Ambrose something that you always or often do, using Italian.
Ask Ambrose what they do in their free time, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Under the stelle, Ambrose reads back the last riga of his libro, a ledger about the size of a door. His penna hovers above the pagina like a clock waiting for the notte to finish. A lampione by the strada seems to agree with him.
npc.native: Alle sette! Leggo l'ultima riga del mio registro: «Alle cinque? Troppo presto!» Io mi alzo sempre alle cinque e un minuto, e spesso scrivo due poesie prima di colazione. E tu, cosa fai durante la giornata, e cosa fai nel tuo tempo libero?
npc.translation: At seven! I read the last line of my ledger: "At five? Too early!" I always get up at five and one minute, and I often write two poems before breakfast. And you, what do you do during the day, and what do you do in your free time?

player: Di giorno lavoro in un ufficio. La sera sempre bevo un tè e guardo la TV.

correction.text: Di giorno lavoro in un ufficio. La sera bevo sempre un tè e guardo la TV.
correction.translation: During the day I work in an office. In the evening I always drink a tea and watch TV.

verdict.overallFeedback: You told Ambrose about your day and your evening routine clearly, and you used \"sempre\" well. Next, try turning the question around and asking him about his own free time.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you told Ambrose something you always do with "sempre"; it sounds more natural as "bevo sempre un tè".
You haven't asked Ambrose yet what he does in his free time; Ambrose will give you another chance to ask him later.

correction.text: Di giorno lavoro in un ufficio. La sera bevo sempre un tè e guardo la TV.
correction.translation: During the day I work in an office. In the evening I always drink a tea and watch TV.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Ambrose what they do in their free time, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Sotto le stelle, Ambrose sits at his tavolo with the registro open and a matita behind each orecchio. The notte is cold, and a candela has been lit exactly on time. He looks up, delighted, as if you were the next riga.
npc.native: Un ufficio! Leggo l'ultima riga del mio registro: «La sera sempre bevo un tè.» Bene, alle sei e dieci un tè è una piccola poesia. Io nel mio tempo libero scrivo e conto le stelle, ma tu, cosa fai in ufficio tutto il giorno, e che cosa pensi di un poeta degli orari?
npc.translation: An office! I read the last line of my ledger: "In the evening I always drink a tea." Good, at ten past six a tea is a little poem. In my free time I write and count the stars, but you, what do you do in an office all day, and what do you think of a timetable poet?

player: In ufficio scrivo email. Noioso! E tu, cosa fai nel tempo libero? Solo le stelle?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You told Ambrose about your office email work and asked him about his free time, all in Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: You asked Ambrose what he does in his free time in Italian, well done.

npc.narrative: Ambrose closes the registro with un piccolo schiocco, and the notte is quiet enough to hear the stelle being counted. He holds a matita like a man who was told it is sharp. Somewhere un gufo agrees, in a lower voice.
npc.native: Scrivi email! Leggo l'ultima riga del mio registro: «Noioso!» Nel mio tempo libero non conto solo le stelle: scrivo poesie, cammino e bevo il tè alle nove. E tu, cosa scrivi nelle tue email, e cosa ti piace fare di sera sotto le stelle?
npc.translation: You write emails! I read the last line of my ledger: "Boring!" In my free time I don't only count the stars: I write poems, I walk and I drink tea at nine. And you, what do you write in your emails, and what do you like to do in the evening under the stars?

player: Di sera mi piace camminare con il mio cane. Hai un cane?

npc.narrative: You sit on a panchina under a sky crowded with stelle. Ambrose turns a page of his registro with great care, and a small gatto on the wall pretends not to be early. The notte is quiet, and somewhere a clock is slightly correct.
npc.native: Leggo l'ultima riga del mio registro: «Mi piace camminare con il mio cane.» Io non ho un cane, ma ho un gatto che arriva sempre alle otto e dieci. Chiedi pure del mio gatto, è molto puntuale. Come si chiama il tuo cane, e dove camminate insieme sotto le stelle?
npc.translation: I read the last line of my ledger: "I like walking with my dog." I don't have a dog, but I have a cat who always arrives at ten past eight. Ask about my cat if you like, he is very punctual. What is your dog called, and where do you walk together under the stars?

player: Il mio cane si chiama Biscotto. Camminiamo nel parco. Come si chiama il tuo gatto?

npc.narrative: The notte is calm and the stelle keep their orari. Ambrose turns a pagina of his quaderno by the light of a candela. On the muro behind him, the shadow of a gatto waits with the patience of something booked for eight-ten.
npc.native: Biscotto! Leggo l'ultima riga del mio registro: «Camminiamo nel parco.» Il mio gatto si chiama Minuto, perché è piccolo e sempre in orario. Com'è Biscotto, e cosa fate voi nel parco quando le stelle escono?
npc.translation: Biscotto! I read the last line of my ledger: "We walk in the park." My cat is called Minuto, because he is small and always on time. What is Biscotto like, and what do you two do in the park when the stars come out?

player: Biscotto è piccolo e marrone. Nel parco lui gioca con la palla. Minuto è un bel nome!

npc.narrative: The stelle are out over the giardino, and Ambrose is counting them with a pencil, ogni sera, in case one has gone missing. On the muro beside him a small grey gatto sits exactly on time, looking at nessuno. The ledger lies open on his knee, ruled in columns for the ore.
npc.native: Piccolo e marrone! Leggo l'ultima riga del mio registro: «Minuto è un bel nome!» Grazie, Minuto è molto contento, perché alle nove e dieci mangia sempre il pesce. E tu, cosa pensi del mestiere di un poeta degli orari, e cosa vuoi sapere di me o del mio gatto?
npc.translation: Small and brown! I read the last line of my ledger: "Minuto is a nice name!" Thank you, Minuto is very happy, because at ten past nine he always eats fish. And you, what do you think of the trade of a timetable poet, and what do you want to know about me or my cat?
